selection.reason: Preregistered ML-vs-ML preference requires same winner on both controlled input spaces; rank reverses. Both methods also leave checker-pattern residuals in an inspected controlled failure case.
selection.recommendation: ML-sRGB is the leading engineering candidate for AM native-image extraction, supported by natural proxy agreement, sRGB controls and observed edges; not a universal or physical-ground-truth winner. Keep comparison settings fixed and discuss declared application scope/failure tolerance before estimator freeze.
not_done: No E7 scene freeze or baseline comparison

visual_review.scope: 20 preselected category-representative black-background crops plus four natural-image seven-background panels and two controlled camel seven-background panels; not exhaustive inspection of all frames/pixels/panels
observations: Naive retains visible pale/gray/colored background contamination in several fur/whisker crops.
ML-sRGB reduces contamination on reviewed natural-image crops; cannot prove physical color truth from proxy match.
ML-linear produces dark/reddish fringes on some natural alpaca/kangaroo crops.
Both ML variants retain checker structure in the controlled camel semi-transparent edge: a real failure under the constructed input, not just disagreement with proxy.
Tiger fine white whisker proxy differences persist; leopard strong cyan coloration is also present in the source/proxy and cannot all be blamed on the estimator.
Do not judge raw foreground at alpha=0, where color is unidentifiable and has no contribution to the composite.

limitations: FG/BG supplied by AM are closed-form estimates; natural-image numbers are proxy consistency only.
Known foreground originates from this proxy distribution; controlled numbers apply to explicitly constructed inputs only.
One of seven background inputs is assigned per source; backgrounds are not seven independent replications.
All scoring recomposites use linear light and optionally encode to sRGB; estimators can use a different working color space.
No native FG arrays archived; deterministic script/config reconstruct estimates; JPG previews never used for metrics.
20 animal categories do not establish human-hair/clothing coverage.
Finite-difference gradient error is not the official matting GRAD implementation.
Timing is CPU process timing under 4-worker concurrency, not standardized efficiency performance.
